title: Sundial trial tally + quick notes (personal)
summary: Compact personal ledger for a set of micro-runs on 'sundial' configs — quick metrics, costs, and TODOs to inform batching/quant choices.
content:
Purpose:
A tiny runbook / tally I use while iterating on sundial kernel + quant profiles. Not a final report — keep minimal columns so I can update mid-run from the terminal.

Legend / notes to self:
- run_id: incremental shorthand (S-###)
- model: alias used in infra (e.g., llama2-13b-q5b)
- quant: quantization profile shorthand (q4_q8, fp16, q5b)
- med_latency_ms: median token decode time measured by tracer (single-request, cold start excluded)
- cost_1k: rough cost per 1k tokens in cents (quick internal calc)
- stable?: rough quality flag after eyeballing 50 samples (Y/N)

Sundial micro-run table (most recent on top):

| run_id | date       | model             | batch | seq | quant  | tokens | med_latency_ms | cost_1k_cents | stable? | notes                                |
|--------|------------|-------------------|-------|-----|--------|--------|----------------|---------------|---------|--------------------------------------|
| S-078  | 2026-03-10 | llama2-13b-v2     | 1     | 512 | q5b    | 1.2k   | 9.4            | 2.6           | Y       | prefix cache hit 30%, nice gen       |
| S-077  | 2026-03-10 | mix-7b-adapter    | 4     | 256 | q4_q8  | 800    | 6.8            | 1.1           | N       | quality drop on long-range; re-eval  |
| S-076  | 2026-03-09 | llama2-70b-plat   | 1     | 1024| fp16   | 2.5k   | 22.1           | 9.8           | Y       | good but costy — try kv cache tweaks  |
| S-075  | 2026-03-08 | llama2-13b-v2     | 2     | 512 | q4_q8  | 1.0k   | 11.7           | 1.9           | ?       | artifacts in codegen; fuzzy metrics   |
| S-074  | 2026-03-07 | distilled-3b      | 8     | 128 | q5b    | 350    | 3.1            | 0.3           | Y       | great throughput, consider for low-cost routes |

Quick observations (actionable):
- q5b on 13b is giving a clean latency win vs q4_q8 without obvious quality loss in prompt set A (S-078 vs S-075). Run more prompts that stress factuality.
- For mix-7b-adapter, batching to 4 reduces per-token latency but introduced hallucination patterns in troubleshooting prompts (see GH PR-412). Flagged as 'N' for stable.
- Distilled-3b continues to be reliable for short sequences — worth a fallback slot in smart routing for cost tier 'cheap'.

Immediate TODOs (prioritized):
- [ ] Expand prompt set to include 30 long-context checks for S-078 (owner: Nola) — target completion 2026-03-14.
- [ ] Add steady-state (warm cache) median numbers for top 3 configs — capture with tracer-run script. (Ethan assigned)
- [ ] Link S-076's warm/cold split to rollout notes in PR-412. (Maya)

Unresolved / questions to triage:
- Are we measuring med_latency_ms consistently? My local tracer ignores queue-time when batch>1. Need to standardize measurement (server-side tracer vs local).
- Cost calc currently uses spot GPU $0.026/hr rounded per token — check with finance for dedicated pricing baseline.

Snippets / command references I keep running:
- quick run (local): sh infra/tools/run_sundial.sh --model llama2-13b-v2 --quant q5b --batch 1 --seq 512 --out /tmp/s-078.json
- collect warm/cold med lat: python infra/trace/summary.py /tmp/s-078.json --warm --percentiles 50,90

Scratch log (random):
- 2026-03-05: tried aggressive KV-sharding (proto) — reduced tail by ~8% but increased median slightly. Worth exploring threshold logic.
- 2026-03-02: noticed two outlier runs with memory GC spikes correlated with other tenant activity on node g12. Put a note for SRE to see if topology change possible.

References / links:
- Quick PR: GH: github.com/redwood-inference/sundial/PR-412  (adapter mix rollback discussion)
- Infra trace helper: /confluence/infra/traces/sundial-howto (draft)
- Slack thread: #infra-infer pinned message (ts=1700000000)

Notes to future me: keep the table very narrow. When it expands into >10 columns it stops being useful as a handheld tally. If multiple people need this, copy to a shared Drive doc and add a changelog column.

End.
